task_instance: Using the mtls-configuration skill's Istio templates, produce the manifests to enable STRICT mesh-wide mTLS, keep a legacy namespace PERMISSIVE for migration, enforce STRICT mTLS on payment-service port 8080 while exempting metrics port 9090, and issue 24h cert-manager workload certificates for payment-service in the production namespace, then apply and verify them.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is to actually configure and verify mutual TLS in a service mesh. Doing that requires a running Kubernetes cluster with a service mesh (Istio/Linkerd), the kubectl/istioctl/linkerd command-line tools, and openssl -- i.e. code/command execution against live infrastructure -- to apply the manifests and verify the handshake (the skill's own verification steps are istioctl authn tls-check, kubectl get peerauthentication/destinationrule, istioctl proxy-config, linkerd viz edges, and openssl cert inspection). This office-assistant runtime cannot run any code or commands and has no cluster, so the manifests cannot be applied or validated. Additionally the API-group identifiers for every manifest's apiVersion field exist only as scrubbed placeholders in this copy of the skill and cannot be guessed, so even the text cannot be made into a parseable manifest. I drafted the structural YAML as text but could not complete, apply, or verify it.
evidence: Read SKILL.md and references/details.md (Templates 1-5 plus certificate-rotation and debugging command blocks). Wrote scenario.md (the concrete task) and mtls-payment-service.yaml (a structural draft tailored from Templates 1 and 3: mesh-wide STRICT PeerAuthentication, PERMISSIVE legacy-namespace override, per-port payment-service policy with 9090 DISABLEd, cert-manager ClusterIssuer + 24h Certificate with renewBefore 8h). Verification was impossible: no code execution, so kubectl apply / istioctl authn tls-check / linkerd viz / openssl could not run; no Kubernetes cluster or service mesh to apply against; and the apiVersion API groups were only scrubbed placeholders, leaving the draft non-parseable.
